new_statements.quote: 2.1.2. У д а р е н и е в Б.я. отсутствует. В Б.я. выделяются четыре фонологических т о н а: ультравысокий (уВ), высокий (В), низкий (Н) и ультранизкий (уН): gba̋ ‛нога’, gbá ‛подарок’, gbà ‛дверь’; pa̋ ‛жалить’, pá ‛наполнять’, pȁ ‛полный’ (о тоновой нотации у разных авторов см. 1.4.0.). Тоны внутри слова могут сочетаться практически в любой последовательности [...]. [p. 13, preface:] Восточная группа манде представлена статьей о боко (Е.В. Перехвальская), написанной по материалам публикаций, в первую очередь Р. Джоунза, но отчасти также А. Про и К. Ведекинда.
new_statements.translation: 2.1.2. There is no stress in Boko. Four phonological tones are distinguished in Boko: extra-high, high, low and extra-low: gba̋ 'leg', gbá 'gift', gbà 'door'; pa̋ 'sting', pá 'fill', pȁ 'full' (on the tone notation of different authors see 1.4.0). Tones within a word can combine in practically any sequence [...]. [Preface, p. 13:] The Eastern Mande group is represented by the article on Boko (E.V. Perekhvalskaya), written from published materials, primarily those of R. Jones, but partly also A. Prost and K. Wedekind.
new_statements.citation: Perekhvalskaya, E.V. 2017. Boko jazyk [Boko]. In: V.F. Vydrin, Yu.V. Mazurova, A.A. Kibrik, E.B. Markus (eds.), Jazyki mira: Jazyki mande [Languages of the World: Mande languages], pp. 1051-1093. St Petersburg: Nestor-Istorija. ISBN 978-5-4469-0824-0.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Boko (the sister language on which the cluster description is based) is described as having no word stress at all; prominence is carried by a four-level lexical/grammatical tone system with free tone combinations inside the word. No statement specific to Bokobaru was found; the chapter names Bokobaru as a separate closely related language and cites its forms only as lexical comparanda.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Related prosodic facts given: an NP may not end in an extra-low tone; extra-high lowers to high/low in tight syntactic contexts; polar questions lengthen the final vowel with extra-low tone; nasalization is a syllable prosody; 'no need to posit a foot' (2.2.1). Vydrin's family overview (p. 34) says stress is absent in most Mande languages.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement ('udarenie.. otsutstvuet'), phrase accent not separately discussed for Boko; statement is for Boko (boko1266), compiled second-hand from Jones 1998, whose description is of Boko with Bokobaru/Busa deviations noted; applicability to Bokobaru (boko1267) is by inference only.
new_statements.first_reading: no word stress according to the source
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is from Perekhvalskaya 2017 'Boko jazyk', which describes BOKO (Glottolog boko1266; Benin and Nigerian Boko), not Bokobaru; the chapter (1.1.2) treats Busa and Bokobaru (boko1267; Kaiama dialect + village Bokobaru/Zogben) as separate closely related languages and cites Bokobaru forms only as comparanda (p. 1053 n. 2). It was compiled from Jones 1998 (which describes Boko with Bokobaru/Busa variations noted as they occur), Prost and Wedekind, without fieldwork (preface p. 13). For boko1266 (also a target with no copies we hold) this saved file is a direct published statement (p. 1053 sec. 2.1.2) and should be routed there. For Bokobaru proper, no first-hand stress statement was opened; Ethnologue 19 (from R. Jones) only says 'tonal'. Sibling check holds Funke 1915 on Busa (dynamic accent on the final syllable of nouns in citation), a different language of the cluster.

sources.note: p. 1053 sec. 2.1.2: 'Udarenie v B.ja. otsutstvuet' (no stress in Boko); four phonological level tones (extra-high, high, low, extra-low) combining freely within the word; p. 1054: NP cannot end in extra-low tone, intonation limited, nasalization syllable-prosodic; 2.2.1: no need to posit a foot. Describes Boko (boko1266); Bokobaru named as a separate sister language; compiled from Jones 1998, Prost, Wedekind (preface p. 13).
